messages:
ops-bot: ALERT - p99 latency spike for /v1/streaming/generate in us-west-2. current p95=0.31s p99=4.2s (SLO p99 2s). detected at 1712345678 via latency-alerts. possible hotspot in continuous batching path (large batches + mixed seq lengths).

alex chen: Im oncall, ack. paging @tara. will start quick mitigations now.

mia r.: +1. Ill pull recent scheduler traces and KV cache eviction logs.

cheng li: seeing a surge of long-seq requests from mobile-prod (seq len 1200-2000). batching window expanded, queues backed up. logs: `batcher.queue_depth -> 18` `avg_batch_size -> 96` in affected hosts.

alex chen: first step - reduce max_batch_size and lower batching window to prioritize latency. applying temporary config.

alex chen: RUN:```
redwoodctl patch pool streaming-usw2 --set max_batch_size=32 --set batch_window_ms=12 --reason "live mitigation p99 spike"
```

deploy-bot: Patch accepted. Rolling change to 6/6 hosts in streaming pool. ETA ~35s. :rocket:

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-20260315-171234 (SLO breach declared). Notifying CS for customer impact assessment.

cheng li: monitor shows immediate drop in avg_batch_size to 28, queue_depth -> 6. p95 now 0.28s. p99 trending down to ~1.1s.

alex chen: OK this looks promising. But still seeing intermittent streaming stalls when mixed long/short sequences co-batch. We should enable seq-length bucketing on the pool to avoid long requests dragging short ones.

mia r.: grabbing scheduler trace: found a scheduling fairness bug where preemption isn't triggered when a long request joins an in-flight batch; we should enable preemptive-shedding flag.

cheng li: Applying bucket + preemptive-shedding. RUN:```
redwoodctl set-pool-policy streaming-usw2 --seqlen-buckets="[0:256,257:1024,1025:9999]" --enable preemptive_shedding=true
```

deploy-bot: Policy update accepted; applying across warm hosts.

alex chen: After both changes, p95=0.24s, p99=0.78s. No streaming stall traces for 2min.

ops-bot: CS notify: 12 customers experienced >2s responses in the window, majority requests recovered with changed config. No request failures.

mia r.: capturing logs for postmortem. collecting `scheduler.trace`, `kvcache.metrics`, and `batcher.debug` from affected hosts.

alex chen: Next steps: keep mitigations for 2hr while we validate fix stability. Create a follow-up ticket to fix preemption logic and add targeted e2e tests for mixed sequence workloads.

tara (sre): Ill take 2hr monitoring and then handle handoff to daytime oncall. @alex please add the list of affected customer ids to INC-20260315-171234.

alex chen: done. added customers + initial timeline + commands used to incident ticket.

mia r.: quick note for PMs: recommend model-client rate limiting for long sequences and a guidance doc for request framing to avoid huge seq lengths in single streaming sessions.

cheng li: also proposing an autoscaling tweak: spin up extra streaming workers when avg_batch_size > 64 and p99>1s to reduce batching pressure. Filing RFC.

alex chen: Handoff: @tara is primary for stabilization and postmortem. if p99 creeps back above 2s, escalate to eng-runtime oncall.

tara (sre): ack, taking over. logging final state: mitigation configs left in place, monitoring alerts suppressed for 20m while we validate. will post postmortem template + timelines. :white_check_mark:

ops-bot: Incident INC-20260315-171234 updated: severity=SEV3, resolved? not yet. will update on postmortem.

alex chen: Thanks team. Quick runbook summary added to thread and ticket.

mia r.: final note: add a synthetic test that mixes 10% long (1k+ tokens) with 90% short to CI gating for batcher changes.

tara (sre): handing off to daytime oncall in 110 minutes. leaving watchlist on.

eng-oncall: thread closed for live mitigation; keep ticket open for root-cause & fix.
